T171: what an ISO-minded evaluator would check. Swept all 117 public pages for certification and compliance language, and the headline result is good AND worth stating precisely, because 'we claim no certifications' is easy to assert and had never been verified: there is NO WorkHive self-certification anywhere - no SOC 2, no ISO 27001, no 'GDPR-compliant', no HIPAA, no PCI-DSS, no bank-grade or military-grade security. All 30 raw hits were a standard the CUSTOMER is audited against (ISO 9001/14001/45001, DOLE OSHS), a PERSON's credential (TESDA NC II/III, CMRP, PSME/IIEE), or the skill matrix's own 'certified level' vocabulary. ★THE ONE REAL OVERCLAIM WAS A CATEGORY ERROR, NOT A BOAST: dole-iso-audit-trail-from-logbook said WorkHive logbook entries 'SATISFY Clause 10.2', the PM dashboard 'SATISFIES Clause 7.1.5', safety observations 'SATISFY Clause 9.1.1'. A clause is satisfied by an ORGANISATION's management system, evidenced by records - a tool holds the evidence, it cannot confer conformity - and the sentence reads as reassurance, so a plant could walk into a surveillance audit believing a feature had covered them. Rewritten to 'gives you the records Clause 10.2 asks you to retain' / 'evidences Clause 9.1.1', plus a callout stating the distinction outright: same value claimed, no false comfort. Live-verified rendering, 0 pageerrors. TWO ASSERTIONS: (clause) no feature may satisfy/meet/fulfil a NUMBERED clause - and note what is deliberately NOT caught, since 'the digital record satisfies three properties' and 'export patterns that satisfy auditors' both appear on that same page and are both fine, because a record CAN satisfy a property and an export CAN satisfy a sampling need; only a numbered clause as the object is the error; (selfcert) no page may claim a certification the platform lacks - zero today, guard-the-absence, because that is the single most tempting sentence to add to a sales page and the most expensive to be wrong about. Teeth proven on both.

T162: a promise to re-check is a promise. The competitor-comparison pages are the most perishable content on the platform and they are written WELL - every competitor price dated ('published entry pricing, August 2026'), sourced ('vendor published pricing and feature pages, accessed August 2026'), caveated ('SaaS pricing moves, confirm current terms with the vendor'), and generous to the competition ('the strongest mobile-first product in the category'). Nothing in the comparisons themselves needed fixing. ★THE RISK IS HIDDEN INSIDE THAT QUALITY: each page also prints 'Pricing verified against vendor and directory listings on 5 August 2026' and 'This comparison is reviewed quarterly for pricing and feature accuracy'. Those are not descriptions, they are COMMITMENTS with a clock running - and left alone they decay into the worst kind of claim, an explicit confident promise of currency printed beside prices nobody has re-checked in a year. A reader trusts the page MORE because of that sentence, which is precisely what makes it expensive when it stops being true. THE ASSERTION: where a page states a verification date AND a review cadence, the date must still be inside the cadence it promised (quarterly = 92 days). Measured 2026-08-26: 3 pages, all verified 5 August 2026, 21 days old and comfortably inside. ★THIS GATE IS BUILT TO GO RED - around 5 November 2026 for these three, unless someone re-verifies. That is the point, not a defect: it converts a marketing sentence into a maintained obligation, and the fix when it fires is a real one (re-check the prices and move the date, or delete the commitment). NO GRACE PERIOD, deliberately - the page names its own cadence, so the cadence is the bar; the passing output prints the days remaining so it arrives as a countdown rather than a surprise. Teeth proven by ageing one date to 5 January: 233d against a 92d promise, exit 1.

T161: content ages with supervision, not heroics. A statistic on a public page is a claim a reader - or an answer engine - will repeat, and the dangerous shape is not an OLD year but a year that silently became a LIE: 'as of 2024, the average plant...' was true when written and is quietly false now, because nobody re-reads a sentence that already shipped. ★THE INVENTORY CHANGED WHAT THIS GATE ASSERTS, and that is the lesson: a first pass across 114 public pages flagged 33 'claims 3+ years old' and nearly every one was a CITATION or a STANDARD EDITION - ISO 14224 (2016), CIBSE Guide D:2015, IEC 62305:2010, DENR DAO 2016-08, Nakajima 1988 for the origin of OEE. Those years are part of the source's IDENTITY; flagging them would have demanded the pages stop citing their standards precisely, the exact opposite of the goal, and 33 false findings on the way. SO IT ASSERTS THE SHAPE, NOT THE AGE. Two things rot and neither is a citation: (as-of) a present-tense claim pinned to a past year - 'as of 2024', 'currently ... 2023', 'latest figures 2022' - allowed only within the current year and the two before it, the window SLIDING with the clock so the gate keeps supervising without anyone re-tuning it; and (future) a statistic dated in a year that has not happened, always a typo or a template copy, which reads as authoritative until someone checks. BOTH ARE ZERO TODAY across 115 pages - this is a guard-the-absence gate in the no-clock-driven-push family, because a property that holds by CARE rather than by structure lapses in silence. Teeth proven on both shapes at once: an injected 'as of 2021' and a '2029 survey' -> 2 flagged, exit 1.

T154: machine-readable truth = human-readable truth. JSON-LD is what an answer engine QUOTES when it cites this platform, and nobody proofreads it because nobody SEES it - so it drifts away from the page underneath and keeps being served, confidently, to the machines that summarize us. TWO CONTRACTS, both born from real drift. FAQ: every FAQPage Question name must appear in the page's visible text - the class T1 caught on the landing page, where the LD still told the provisioning-waitlist story after the page had moved to instant signup; an FAQ rich result PROMISES the page answers that question, so if the words are not there the promise is to content that does not exist (508 questions across 115 public pages, all present). NAME: an Article headline must still be recognisable as the page's own og:title/<title> - FOUND HERE, predictive-alert-thresholds-plants had been retitled to lead with 'ISO 10816 Vibration Thresholds and Predictive Alert Limits', a deliberate move toward the citable standard, while its LD headline kept the older vaguer 'Predictive Alert Thresholds for Industrial Plants', so an answer engine reading the structured data got the version WITHOUT the ISO anchor that makes the page worth citing (synced; 53 headlines now match). ★HowToStep NAMES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT GATED, AND THE EXCLUSION IS THE FINDING: a first pass flagged 31 'gaps' across 12 HowTo pages and every one was editorial paraphrase - the OEE guide's LD says 'Measure planned production time' where the page heads that section 'Step 1: Planned Production Time'. Same step, different register. A step name is a LABEL for a procedure; demanding substring identity would have shipped 31 false findings and taught everyone to ignore this gate. The FAQ question and the headline are different in kind - both are read VERBATIM by their consumers, so identity is the actual contract there. Teeth proven on BOTH halves: a fabricated question and a reverted headline, 2 flagged, exit 1.

T158: a canonical must name a URL that EXISTS. rel=canonical is a claim - 'the real version of this page lives here' - and when the URL it names does not exist, the page tells every crawler its authoritative copy is at nothing. FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-26, VERIFIED AGAINST PRODUCTION rather than inferred: workhiveph.com/workhive/public-feed.html returned 404 while workhiveph.com/public-feed.html returned 200, and FIFTEEN pages shipped the dead form - a /workhive/ segment left over from an earlier deploy path, still being served long after the site moved to the domain root. ★WHY IT SURVIVED EVERY EXISTING CHECK: they all asked whether a canonical was PRESENT, and all 15 were present, well-formed, absolute and unique - and pointed at a 404. Presence is the easy half of a claim; this gate checks the half that costs something. ★THE ONE THAT MATTERED MOST was public-feed, the anonymous shop window and the only one of the 15 meant to be found by strangers: a shared link to it carried a signal saying the real page was elsewhere, at a URL that does not resolve. Now 145 on-site canonicals all name a page that exists. STATIC BY DESIGN - the path IS the defect, and a live HTTP check would make the gate depend on the network to state a fact about a string. TEETH PROVEN by re-breaking public-feed's canonical: 1 flagged, exit 1.

T160: the SEO funnel must not jump while you read it. CLS is where a page loses a searcher without erroring - text settles, the reader's eye is already moving, and the line they were on is somewhere else - and on the funnel it costs twice, because Core Web Vitals feed ranking, so the pages most dependent on search were the ones shifting. MEASURED, ISOLATED, THEN FIXED. The learn template shifted 0.384 CLS at 390, nearly 4x the 0.1 bar. ★THE RECORDED SUSPICION WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAID SO: the note blamed an element injected at ~1s, and a MutationObserver armed alongside the shift observer recorded NO insertion of any size. The timeline showed a 0.182 shift at 903ms and document.fonts.ready at 907ms; blocking the font stylesheet took CLS to 0.000 while blocking the Tailwind CDN only reached 0.156. The font swap was the whole cause. THE FIX was one parameter - display=swap to display=optional across 113 public pages: optional gives the font ~100ms then never swaps, so the page cannot jump, and measured on a real load it STILL renders Poppins. The only reader who now sees the fallback is on a genuinely slow first load, which is exactly the reader who previously got the jump instead. Verified 0.000 CLS across learn, tools and the landing page. ★IT ASSERTS THE PARAMETER, NOT A CLS NUMBER: a lab CLS reading on loopback is optimistic and noisy, and a gate that fails intermittently gets ignored - the parameter is deterministic and it IS the defect.

T3/T153: the calculator pages state the account requirement. The 60 /tools/ pages are the top of the funnel - a searcher looking for 'OEE calculator' lands on one, and what it promises decides whether the next click is trust or a bounce. MEASURED 2026-08-26 and the human-facing story is HONEST: none of the 60 embeds a calculator (they are landing pages that explain a calculation and hand off) and every one says so plainly - 'free with a WorkHive account. Sign-up takes about 30 seconds.' ZERO still carry the 'no sign-up needed' claim T3 recorded, which linked into a gated page and was false twice over. The gate keeps a fixed claim fixed, because that wording lived in a TEMPLATE - it came back everywhere at once when it came back at all. ★A RECORDED FINDING IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ENFORCE: every one of the 60 declares JSON-LD @type SoftwareApplication with an Offer of price 0 and a url pointing at the LANDING page, so a search or answer engine reads 'there is a free web application here', follows the url, and finds a page about an application that lives somewhere else. The human CTA is honest; the MACHINE claim overclaims. Pointing that url at the app would make it true in one line, but rewriting the structured data of 60 pages changes how the platform is presented in search - an outward-facing decision nobody can quietly reverse - so it is written up for Ian rather than done. Teeth-proven by restoring the exact old wording.

T156: a shared link should look intentional. T125 established what sharing here actually looks like - workers paste links into Viber and Messenger group chats - which makes the Open Graph card the first thing most people see of a page, often before the page itself. THE FINDING: 60 of ~116 public pages shipped NO og:image and no twitter:card, and they were all the /tools/ CALCULATORS - the top of the funnel, the pages most likely to be shared by a worker who just used one. Every one rendered as a bare grey link while the learn cluster's 53 articles rendered a proper card. public-feed had an image and a title but no og:description, so its card showed a headline, a picture, and whatever text the platform chose to guess. Fixed by reusing the SAME asset the learn cluster already uses rather than inventing a second one: two social images drift and one ends up stale. ★IT CHECKS THE IMAGE FILE EXISTS, not merely that the tag does - a card pointing at a missing PNG renders exactly like a card with no image, and the tag being present makes it look handled, which is the worst combination because nobody re-checks a field that is filled in. App pages are deliberately out of scope: a signed-in surface behind an auth wall is not shared to a group chat. Teeth-proven both ways - card removed RED, image pointed at a missing file RED.

T152: the teaching cluster is navigable in BOTH directions. 53 articles only teach as a cluster if a reader can move through them, and two different failures break that while being invisible to each other. AN ORPHAN is an article no hub link reaches: it exists, it is indexed, a searcher can land on it, and nobody browsing the library will ever find it - writing it was work that reaches nobody. A DEAD END is an article that links onward to nothing: a reader who finishes it has to go back and start again, which is where a session ends. Measured: 53 articles, 53 reachable from the hub, ZERO orphans, ZERO dead ends, and the hub links to nothing missing. The gate keeps it that way, because adding an article and forgetting the hub entry is a one-line omission nobody notices. ★IT ALSO CHECKS THE REVERSE OF AN ORPHAN - a hub link to an article that does not exist - because a library index offering a guide that 404s is worse than not listing it, and this cluster has been renamed before. ★AND ONWARD LINKS MUST REACH OTHER LEARN ARTICLES, not merely somewhere: a page whose only outbound link is a signup CTA is a dead end for a reader who came to learn, however many links it technically has. Teeth-proven by renaming one hub slug, which fired BOTH arms at once - the article became an orphan and the hub gained a promise it could not keep.

T151: a searcher's question answered above the fold, swept across all 53 learn articles. Somebody arrives from a search result with a question the snippet promised this page answers; what they meet in the first screen decides whether they stay, and the failure mode is not a broken page but one that opens with throat-clearing and buries the answer four scrolls down. ★THE ORACLE IS ANSWER-PRESENCE, NOT META-VERBATIM - T151 learned that the hard way when an earlier pass checked whether the meta description's words appeared on the page and produced a false red, because a description SUMMARIZES rather than quotes. Four assertions per article: an H1 exists; substantive opening prose follows it; that opening carries a distinctive term from the title; and a freshness stamp is visible, because a searcher landing on undated maintenance guidance cannot tell if it is current. ★THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS BEFORE ANY VERDICT WAS TRUSTED, each found by READING the flags rather than acting on them: a {3,} filter silently dropped this platform's most important short terms (PM, AI, OEE) so an article opening 'Most Philippine plants run PMs' read as off-topic; an exact match called 'measurement' a miss for a title saying 'Measuring'; and scanning only

elements flagged the WorkHive-vs-MaintainX page, which opens with a textbook answer ('Choose MaintainX if... Choose WorkHive if...') written in a

of lines - the

tags it found were the byline and a repeated pricing disclaimer, so the gate read the furniture and missed the answer. It now reads VISIBLE TEXT, and allows one paragraph of runway, because enforcing sentence-one would legislate prose style rather than measure arrival. All 53 pass. Mutation-proven both ways: burying an answer behind preamble goes RED, and stripping a freshness stamp goes RED.

T133: absent is not zero, especially in pesos. whFmtPeso exists for one recorded reason - Number(null) is 0 and finite, so a null amount slips through as a confident 0.00. A filed top-up of PHP300 once rendered as PHP0.00 and a ledger line of unknown value rendered as +0, a sentence saying the entry moved nothing. The helper prints a GAP for absent and still prints 0 for a real zero, because a person can act on 'we do not know' and cannot act on a wrong number. T18: a read-gate must not depend on an event that may never fire. skillmatrix gates its exam behind 'read the lesson first' - the Take-exam button starts disabled and a scroll handler enables it once the reader reaches the bottom. Correct intent, and it had a hole: the button was enabled ONLY from inside that handler. ★A LESSON WHOSE CONTENT FITS THE BOX NEVER SCROLLS, so the scroll event never fires, checkScroll never runs, and the reader is left in front of a permanently disabled 'Take exam' beside a hint telling them to scroll something that does not scroll - with no way out of that screen but closing it. Latent only because every lesson written so far happens to overflow, and lesson bodies are AUTHORED CONTENT, so the first short one ships the trap to whoever writes it. FIXED by evaluating the gate once at open, after the scroll reset: self-correcting, because for a non-scrolling box scrollTop + clientHeight already exceeds scrollHeight - 80 so the check passes immediately, while a long lesson at scrollTop 0 still fails it and the gate holds. ★VERIFIED LIVE ON BOTH BRANCHES, since the risk of this fix is that it opens the gate for everyone: long content (scrollHeight 822 vs clientHeight 502) still reports disabled=true with the hint shown, short content (54 vs 54) reports disabled=false with the hint cleared, 0 pageerrors. ★AND THE GATE ITSELF FAILED ITS FIRST TEETH TEST: the invocation count matched `function checkScroll()` - the DECLARATION - so deleting the real call still left a count of 1 and it reported PASS on the exact defect it exists for. A negative lookbehind for 'function ' fixed it; the teeth test refusing to go red is the only reason that was caught. Narrow by design: this is one known control, and inferring 'enabled only by an event' across the platform would be guessing at intent.

T159: the page must say which language it is in. A screen reader picks its pronunciation rules from <html lang>, so Filipino text announced under lang='en' comes out as English phonemes applied to Tagalog - not accented, but unrecoverable. WCAG 3.1.1 asks for the page's language and 3.1.2 that a change of language be marked. ★THE HARD HALF IS THAT THIS PLATFORM IS BILINGUAL BY TOGGLE, NOT BY URL: one page, _t(en, fil) at every string, and a wh_lang preference - so the declaration is not a static fact set at build time, it has to FOLLOW the toggle, which is exactly the half a static audit misses. MEASURED and the discipline is clean: all 156 public pages declare <html lang> (none silent); utils.js:219 sets documentElement.lang from the stored locale on EVERY page load, so a reader who chose Filipino gets the right declaration even on pages with no translation engine of their own; and all three pages that WRITE wh_lang (index, analytics, analytics-report) also assign documentElement.lang in their toggle handler, so switching mid-session updates the declaration without a reload. TWO ASSERTIONS: every public page carries <html lang>, and any page that writes the wh_lang preference must also assign documentElement.lang - a toggle that changes the words while leaving the declaration behind is WORSE than no toggle, because the page then asserts a language it is not in. ★NO hreflang IS ASSERTED, deliberately rather than by omission: hreflang describes ALTERNATE URLs for the same content and this platform has none - the locale lives in localStorage, so /learn/x is one URL serving whichever language the reader chose, and demanding hreflang would be demanding a second site. Whether to publish a Filipino public corpus at all is T159's open posture question and Ian's to answer; this gate holds the part that is true under either answer. Teeth proven on both halves.

T111: comms held to the same bar as the glass. The DP manipulation-absence dims are measured on PAGES, so EMAIL escapes them entirely - and it is the one surface that reaches a person who may not even have an account, cannot be corrected once sent, and is where urgency-shaped copy is most tempting and least visible to any UI test. That fix shipped with no gate. Teeth-proven three ways: the pre-fix footer (both arms RED), an injected 'Your hive needs you - act now' (RED), and a new un-audited resend-calling function (RED).

T109: the structural reason this platform needs no quiet hours YET, guarded so it stays true. The walk found no quiet-hours machinery anywhere AND - the part that mattered - nothing that CLAIMS it, so the platform is silent rather than lying. What makes that absence defensible is measurable: EVERY push producer is EVENT-DRIVEN (mention, reply, best answer, assignment, approval decision, report, submission, service completion). Not one is clock-driven, so a phone cannot buzz at 3am unless somebody in that hive acted at 3am - which on a round-the-clock plant is a night shift and is legitimate news. The day a scheduled digest or nightly reminder ships that stops being true instantly, because a clock-driven push CHOOSES its own hour, and choosing 3am for someone is precisely what quiet hours exist to prevent. Asserts no cron job invokes anything that enqueues a push - a DB function calling enqueue_user_push (checked transitively one hop, since fanout_completion_push is reached through a trigger) or an edge function that does. notify-push and the outbox drain are exempt BY NAME: they deliver what is already queued, decide nothing, and must run every minute or nothing arrives. THIS GATE IS MEANT TO FIRE ONE DAY - when the digest T106 records as a scoped decision gets built, it goes red, and the red is the point: it forces the quiet-window question to be answered BEFORE the first scheduled push reaches a phone. Mutation-proven by scheduling a 3am-PHT digest cron: caught by name, then unscheduled. SKIPs without docker.

Neither had fired - the receiver fails closed without its signing secret and the breaker needs Resend to be failing - so both were latent, primed to go off at the first real bounce after Ian sets the secret and at the first email outage. The wallet card called provider_credit_balance() instead — the ledger sum alone — and labelled it the balance, so a seller with live listings saw a number larger than they could spend, on the same page that had just told them listing would hold some of it. The total stays; the HELD figure is added beside it, and renders only when something is actually held (a 'reserved ₱0' on every wallet teaches people to stop reading the card). ★MEASURED LIVE: credit_reservations is empty on this stack, so the gate CREATES a 50-credit hold inside a transaction and rolls it back — available=-50, reserved=50, total=0, split exact, 0 rows left. The probe row references a real listing because the table enforces num_nonnulls(listing_id, request_id)=1. PERSONA TASK-SUCCESS - can a DIVERSE human finish the money task, not just an idealised one? (Ian 2026-07-31: consider the diversity of human beings.) Every journey in the bank implicitly walked a competent, sighted, literate, English-reading, fast-network, calm user, and almost none of this platform's real users are all six at once - PH plant technicians in their fifties, first-time e-wallet users, someone outdoors in glare wearing gloves, someone on 3G. DIVERSITY IS NOT A PAGE PROPERTY, it is WHO IS WALKING, so it lives on the journey axis. DIVISION OF LABOUR, deliberately: UFAI grades the PAGE (validate_service_ufai_deep measures 390/1280 tap targets and overflow), validate_i18n_coverage owns language, validate_clickable_keyboard_a11y owns keyboard - none can answer 'could THIS PERSON complete THIS TASK'. The 25 personas and their journey pairings live in tools/service_personas.mjs as RUNTIME CONDITIONS (viewport, zoom, colour filter, throttle, locale, input delay), not comments, and 129 unpaired combinations are recorded WITH REASONS rather than dropped - 25 personas x 7 families is 175 walks nobody runs, and an unrunnable matrix silently becomes an unrun one. Seven checks on the families where failure costs pesos: 12 states carry DISTINCT TEXT labels not colour alone (P-COLORBLIND); the release screen discloses who gets what, that the platform never holds the money, and what happens if the job was bad (P-SCAMWARY, the persona who decides whether this economy works at all); the min-balance refusal is announced AND says how to fix it (P-UNBANKED); the release resists a double tap (P-IMPULSIVE); money terms are translatable (P-FILIPINO); the map has a text equivalent, since a map is unusable by a screen reader and without a list discovery is closed entirely (P-SCREENREADER); and a 48px target floor (P-GLOVED, a real industrial constraint). ITS OWN FIRST TWO READINGS WERE INSTRUMENT BUGS: it reported the 12 status labels MISSING because its regex assumed quoted object keys while the source uses bare ones, and reported the min-balance refusal owed because it read only marketplace.html while the message lives on marketplace-seller.html. Both are fixed and both are why it now reads the real SVC_CHIP mapping across BOTH money surfaces instead of pattern-matching one.

PAYMENT RAILS - three GCash accounts meet in this product and only ONE of them may ever be on a given screen. WorkHive has no business registration and therefore no merchant account, so every rail is a PERSONAL number: a buyer pays the PROVIDER's own GCash directly and the platform never touches it; a provider tops up credits by paying the FOUNDER's personal 0995 009 2416; a credits spend moves no GCash at all, being a ledger transfer between two wallets. THE INVARIANT: the founder's number may appear ONLY on the provider's top-up card. Put it on a buyer-facing payment step and the buyer sends job money to a person who is not party to the job, cannot fulfil it, and cannot reconcile it against any request - and NOTHING ERRORS. The money is not lost to a bug but to a stranger's honest reading of the screen, which is worse, because nobody finds out until the provider asks where their payment is. This is also the exact friction Ian named by hand ('I want it hassle free for my users, like the hassle of payment two gcash accounts'): a buyer must see exactly one number, the provider's. Four assertions: every occurrence of the founder number sits on an allowed surface; no buyer-facing payment surface contains it in ANY spacing or punctuation (the regex tolerates '0995 009 2416', '0995-009-2416' and '09950092416' as one number); the buyer's confirm step states that WorkHive holds no money, which is the sentence a wary first-timer actually decides on; and that step names the PROVIDER as payee so 'who do I pay' has one answer where it is asked. Comments and doc blocks are stripped before matching - only RENDERED strings can mislead a person. Teeth: planting the founder's number on marketplace.html's payment step makes this FAIL naming that surface and that consequence; selftest proves all four failures are caught and a correct topology passes. Static, fast, no DB.

CL ui-visual CONTRAST on every production page, populated - BOTH oracles, run on the platform's OWN two calibrated lenses (live-state-runner's composited APCA + axe's WCAG) rather than a third implementation. It settles the 78 rows the bank had owed behind a recorded belief that contrast is 'NOT computable from the CSSOM here' - true of the NAIVE probe that produced it (uncomposited alpha reads ratio 1.00, a gradient defeats a single-colour sample) and false of this one, which composites alpha up the ancestor chain, averages gradient stops, resolves background-clip:text, and reports candidates/truncated so a cap can never hide under '0 failing'. IT WAS AN ORPHAN: built, working, and invokable from NOWHERE - registered in no suite and absent from PROVERS - so it enforced nothing for months while reporting 0 failing across 22 pages on the strength of a teeth claim that was a COMMENT ABOUT A DIFFERENT FILE'S MATHS. Baseline: 22 pages, 2503 APCA nodes, 0 failing, nothing truncated. Reports carry teethRun so a teeth run can never be misread as a measurement - a mistake made once here.

Same two lenses, same teeth (2/2 views caught the planted violator on both). Baseline: 37 targets reached, 36 graded, 1151 nodes, 0 failing. HIVE-CAPTURE INVARIANT — a load-time hive capture is only safe while nothing can change the active hive mid-page. marketplace.html does `const HIVE_ID = whHiveId()` once at load and stamps it on every hail and listing, so if the active hive could change while the page is open, work would be filed into the WRONG TENANT. It cannot today: the only pages that write `wh_active_hive_id` are hive.html (the switcher) and index.html (the sign-in bootstrap), and reaching the marketplace from either is a full page load, so the const is always read fresh. That was recorded as the A4 finding on `TB-A345-architecture-quality` — no defect — and it is a conclusion resting on an invariant nobody enforced: add an in-page hive switcher to the marketplace and every subsequent hail carries a stale tenant id with no test going red. Per this platform's disposition rule, a covered-by-nature cell still gets a gate asserting the contract it rests on. TWO ASSERTIONS: (A) the WRITER ALLOWLIST — exactly hive.html and index.html may write the key, and a third page appearing goes red with the instruction to re-check capture scope on every page that reads it, because adding a writer is a decision rather than automatically a bug; (B) THE CAPTURING PAGES MUST NOT WRITE IT — marketplace.html / marketplace-seller.html / marketplace-admin.html must contain zero writers, which is the live-bug condition, since a writer in the same document can run after the capture. CHECKING THE PREMISE CORRECTED THE FINDING TWICE, both errors mine: the cell claimed every write lives on hive.html (index.html:2953 writes it too — the conclusion survived, the stated premise was false), and index.html ALSO reads whHiveId() into a `const HIVE_ID`, which looks like the same stale-capture shape but is not, because that capture is FUNCTION-scoped inside the ops-home renderer (re-read per call) and the write is deliberately followed by `_initDashboard(...)` to re-render against the new hive — verified by reading both sites rather than trusting the comment. So the distinction that matters is SCOPE, not filename. The gate deliberately does NOT try to compute JS scope from a regex: brace and regex-literal counting over inline script is the brittle-validator trap this platform has already been bitten by, so it asserts the two cheap, unarguable properties instead. Self-test injects a writer into marketplace.html THROUGH THE READER (no file on disk is touched, the same discipline as injecting a mutant inside a transaction) and requires the gate to go red naming that page — without it, a green result would mean nothing. Static file scan, fast, always runs.

LIFECYCLE STATE REACHABILITY (§10 MK4) — every state in a `status` CHECK must be both SURFACED and REACHABLE. A CHECK vocabulary is a promise about what the product does, and it breaks two ways, silently in both directions because unreachable code raises nothing. FOUND 2026-07-29: `marketplace_listings.sold` is fully dressed — a blue 'Sold' chip, a `.listing-item.sold` border rule, a schema.org/SoldOut mapping in the runtime JSON-LD, and `recompute_seller_sales_and_tier` COUNTS listings WHERE status='sold' to drive the seller's tier — and NOTHING anywhere writes it. A seller who sells something cannot say so, and the tier that counts sales counts a number that is always zero. (The mirror case is already recorded as a schema question for Ian: the same table carries moderation_reason/moderated_at/moderated_by with no `rejected` in its vocabulary — a consumer with no state.) THE PRODUCER TEST UNIONS THREE SIGNALS because none alone is right: the DERIVED guard matrix (a guard's allow-list only covers USER writes, missing `accepted` via the workhive.service_system_write bypass and `expired` via the sweep cron), a DB assignment (`SET status =` / `status :=` ONLY — matching `status = 'x'` anywhere counts WHERE-clause READS as writes, which produced a FALSE PASS on the one real finding twice in a row), and a page write including the literal passed as an ARGUMENT (the seller advances a job through `svcAdvance(id, next)`, so a payload-only test calls seven wired states unreachable). Forward-only: the known gap is NAMED in lifecycle_reachability_baseline.json and still prints every run; a NEW unreachable or invisible state FAILs. Self-test proves both baseline directions.

OFFLINE WRITE GUARD — a user-triggered write must REFUSE before it fires, not after. C12 (SERVICE_HAILING_ROADMAP §4b) durable side-effects: a boundary-crossing effect must survive a consumer that is down. 12 live invariants over `service_outbox` + the `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` relay: schema/RLS/no-client-grant · enqueue+drain+reconcile are EXECUTE-revoked (a DEFINER helper is user-callable BY DEFAULT — this arc already shipped one live IDOR from that) · enqueue is a plain INSERT so it commits iff the transition does (an HTTP call inside the transition tx is the coupling the outbox removes) · a failed delivery is pushed OUT in time, not retried hot · a payload past max_attempts DEAD-LETTERS instead of looping · nothing is stranded 'in_flight' · SOMETHING ACTUALLY CALLS THE FAN-OUT · and a real enqueue→relay→2xx→done round-trip, minted and swept by the gate itself (residue is not evidence). WHY THE BLUNT ONES: Web Push shipped fully built and NEVER INVOKED — subscriptions, sw.js handler, VAPID, subscribe UI and notify-push all existed while no caller did, so providers subscribed and received nothing. 'Built but never called' must never be green again. Skips if docker/psql is absent.

T123 (2026-08-28): whitespace must never decide whether the system works. People paste - a part number from a Viber message, a username from an email - and every pasted value can carry a leading or trailing space the person cannot see. Where the value is used for IDENTITY or MATCHING, that invisible character decides the outcome: a space on si-username/su-username and sign-in fails with correct credentials; a space in the inventory SEARCH and a part that exists returns nothing, which reads as 'we do not stock it' to someone standing at the shelf; a space in part_number/part_name on WRITE is baked into the record, so the row never matches its own search again; a space on a recipient email and the report bounces. All six are trimmed today and this holds them there. ★THE PROPERTY IS DELIBERATELY NOT 'TRIM EVERYTHING': dayplanner's note and logbook's knowledge field are textareas where a person may indent lines, so leading whitespace is CONTENT, and a gate demanding .trim() on every text field would enforce an opinion about prose and eventually be switched off. ★THE SCAN NEEDED CAREFUL READING, WHICH IS WHY THE SUBJECT LIST IS EXPLICIT: a search for untrimmed values reaching a payload flagged inventory's q and cat, both of which are the remembered-filter SNAPSHOT - restored into the input and re-trimmed at the point of use - so judging by the assignment rather than the use would have filed two defects against correct code. ★AND THE SELFTEST MUTATES COPIES, NEVER DISK: its first version rewrote the real product files and restored them in a finally block, which is one crash or one concurrent board read away from a corrupted source or a voided board. Selftest 7/7, each field mutated independently.

T134 (2026-08-28): a listing's photo leaves the public bucket when the listing does - and when it is REPLACED. Deleting a listing removed the row and left the JPEG at a permanent public URL, so 'this cannot be undone' was true of the row and quietly false of the photo: anyone holding the link still had it after the seller believed they had removed the listing. ★THE FIX-EVERY-PATH PASS FOUND THE BIGGER SOURCE - deleting is rare, REPLACING an image on edit is common, and it orphaned the old object exactly the same way, far more often. A gate holding only the delete path would have locked the half that almost never runs while the frequent one kept leaking, which is worse than no gate because the board would report the class closed. Holds both sites and both of the edit path's guards: remove only when the URL actually CHANGED (re-saving an unchanged listing must not delete its own live image) and only when the old object is OURS by bucket-marker (a seller may paste an external URL, and we must not reach into someone else's host). Both cleanups stay BEST-EFFORT and wrapped, running after the write so a storage hiccup can never cost the seller the edit or delete they asked for - the inverse of the coupling T12 had to break. Selftest 5/5. ★THE OWNERSHIP NEGATIVE WAS VACUOUS FIRST: a whole-file search for indexOf(_marker) is satisfied by the DELETE path's own copy, so removing the EDIT path's guard left the file matching and the case passed while detecting nothing - two near-identical blocks on one page is precisely the shape that makes a loose check vacuous, and it is now scoped to the edit block.

T165 (2026-08-28): the privacy policy must describe the analytics that actually ship. It said 'we do not run third-party analytics... when we add web analytics in the future, this page will be updated' while GA4 (wh-ga4.js) was already live on 10 public pages. ★A STALE SENTENCE ON A LEGAL SURFACE IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF DEFECT: everywhere else drift means a number is wrong or a label is old, but here it means the document a regulator, an enterprise buyer or a worker reads to decide whether to trust us was making a FALSE STATEMENT about what we collect - false in the direction that flatters us, which is the direction nobody audits, and invisible because prose never looks broken. Gated as PARITY in both directions so it cannot rot from either side: if wh-ga4.js loads, the policy must NAME Google Analytics and must not carry the future-tense denial; it must state the IP anonymization the code actually runs (naming GA4 without it under-claims our own protection, which is still a mismatch); and if GA4 were ever removed, a policy still describing it over-claims what is collected - the same drift in reverse. Comment-stripped, and that is not a formality here: the fix left an HTML comment quoting the old denial verbatim so the correction stays legible, and a detector reading comments would find 'when we add web analytics in the future' in the FIXED file and convict the page for documenting its own repair - the single most reliable false positive in this whole gate family, hit three times on other subjects this session. Selftest 6/6, including a non-vacuity check that the GA4 page roster is not empty.

MASKED BY DEFAULT: every password field ships type=password, and the shared whPrompt honours inputType:'password' end to end - which had a real gap, since _mount read inputType but whPrompt built its own options object and never forwarded it, so a caller asking for a masked prompt silently got a plain text box and a secret was typed in the clear on a shared plant tablet. The caller was correct; the plumbing dropped it with nothing looking wrong. REVEAL MUST SPEAK: a show/hide toggle is a usability necessity because people mistype passwords on phones, but a control that silently changes whether a secret is visible is a shoulder-surfing hazard for exactly the person who cannot check by looking - so it must flip BOTH aria-label (what pressing it does next) and aria-pressed (what state it is in now). ★AND THE GATE ANCHORS ON THE ACCESSIBLE NAME RATHER THAN THE CODE SHAPE FOR A MEASURED REASON: a search for controls flipping an input type found ZERO, twice, because the pattern expected a quoted literal and togglePwd assigns a TERNARY. The three aria-labels reading 'Show password' were the only evidence the toggles existed - the accessible name was what the code-shape search could not see. Selftest 8/8.

T53 (2026-08-28): a person who only READS is never forced to write. Not every account operates the plant - a manager, an owner, a client on a site visit signs in to LOOK, reads, and leaves. That lane had no gate, because every existing journey asserts that an ACTION succeeds, and an action-shaped oracle cannot see this persona's defect: being stopped before reading anything at all. ★THE TRAJECTORY SPLITS AND ONLY HALF IS GATEABLE: whether the exec deserves a different LANDING is a design call and stays Ian's; whether a reader is FORCED INTO A WRITE is observable on arrival and needs no decision. Walks six exec-shaped surfaces signed in, settles, and requires no blocking modal, no body-scroll lock, no sign-in/pick-a-hive wall, no focus stolen into a text input (on a phone that opens a keyboard at someone who came to read), and no page error. ★THE SIXTH CLAUSE IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE, because the other five are all ABSENCES and a BLANK PAGE satisfies every one of them - an all-absence oracle grades a dead page as a perfect reading experience. So it also requires the reader actually got words, counting VISIBLE TEXT rather than figures: T53's own walk twice misread a healthy surface as thin, once by counting characters mid-render and once by counting figures on analytics-report, whose correct state is an instruction with no figures at all. The 220-char floor is deliberately low for exactly that page. Read-only by construction - never clicks, types or submits. 6/6 green at 1280. Teeth 5/5 via --teeth: each clause injected on a real signed-in page and asserted to fire, each checked non-vacuous (the clean page reported 0 first), because a gate locking already-correct behaviour has never been seen to go red and is otherwise a green light of unknown wiring.

T121 (2026-08-28): a dismissal is a person's decision, not the browser's. The shared station tablet is this platform's normal deployment - one device, a crew signing in and out through a shift - and three dismissal flags stored the literal string '1', which belongs to the BROWSER: wh_onboarding_dismissed (index's first-run Getting Started ladder), wh_cmms_guide_dismissed (integrations' setup guide), and wh_guide_link_dismissed_<page> (learn-link's 'New to this page?' chip, which rides EVERY page). Worker A taps Dismiss; worker B signs in on the same tablet and is never introduced to anything. ★THIS LEAK RUNS THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION FROM ITS SIBLINGS, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED THEM: the draft, filter and companion-history fixes all stopped A's CONTENT reaching B, so they read as privacy work and this did not - nothing of A's is exposed. What crosses is A's DECISION, and the cost lands on B as an ABSENCE: no card, no chip, nothing on screen to notice or report. The onboarding ladder made it sharper still - its three step-checks were ALREADY person-aware (workerName, jobs, pmDoneToday), so the card knew B had done nothing; it just never got to run, because the flag returned before the check. Correct logic behind a device-wide gate. Fixed centrally (whStateOwner/whIsDismissed/whSetDismissed in utils.js, replacing a FOURTH hand-rolled owner read) and at all three sites; a legacy '1' is nobody's, so the guide returns once - for HELP that is the safe direction, since re-showing a card costs a tap and hiding it costs the introduction. sessionStorage flags are exempt: they die with the tab. Live-proven at 390 (A dismissed -> B sees the guide -> A still dismissed -> legacy '1' belongs to no one), probe restoring the real owner it captured first. Selftest 9/9, including two non-vacuity checks: the first versions of both negatives swapped only the helper CALL, leaving the typeof guard inside the exemption window, so they passed while detecting nothing.

CF: an optional API's absence must never hide CONTENT (T119, 2026-08-27). MEASURED by removing the capability an older engine lacks: index.html styled `.reveal { opacity: 0 }` and made those elements visible only when an IntersectionObserver callback added `.visible`, so on an engine without the API the constructor THREW, the rest of that script block never ran, and all 14 .reveal elements stayed invisible permanently - the landing page rendered 525 characters of text where every other page rendered 1146+. ★NOTHING WOULD HAVE REPORTED IT: no failed request, no error state, no blank shell - the page 'loaded fine' and simply never faded its content in, the same shape as a skeleton that never resolves. And the source SAID it was safe; the comment above the observer read 'all browsers', which is an assumption wearing the clothes of a check. ★THE GATE REQUIRES BOTH HALVES, because a guard alone is not enough: skipping the observer while leaving opacity:0 in place would pass a naive 'is it guarded' test and still ship a blank page. So every construction must have a feature check BEFORE it - positionally, since a check that runs after the throw protects nothing - AND the hidden class must have a reveal-everything fallback. Fixed at all five call sites, each failing OPEN: the main reveal shows everything, the stagger reuses its EXISTING reducedMotion branch rather than inventing a second path, the before/after rows are shown outright, and the sticky-CTA and nav-highlight observers (which only ADD behaviour) return early - the nav one was the loudest, constructing an observer PER SECTION. Verified both ways: without the API index renders 1061 chars and nothing throws; with it, .reveal still gains .visible on scroll. Teeth 4/4.

CF: a flow's OPENED state must fit the floor viewport, not just the page at rest (T113, 2026-08-27). ★THE GAP: control-within-viewport walks 16 pages AT REST, but the controls that decide whether work gets RECORDED do not exist at rest - the PM completion sheet, the deferral control, the add-task sheet are built or revealed mid-flow, and each is a different layout from the page hosting it. The resting sweep can be green over every page while the Save button of the sheet a worker must press sits off the edge: the same class T113 already found twice, one interaction deeper than any resting check can reach. Walks T10 (complete a PM, and its honest alternative - record a DEFERRAL) and T13 (the clock-in handover read) at 320. ★IT ARRIVES THE WAY A WORKER DOES: alert-hub hands pm-scheduler an ?asset=, the detail opens, and a REAL scope item's mark-done control is clicked. An earlier cut called openSheet() by hand and measured an EMPTY sheet - the same seven controls whatever the task, because markDone() is what fills in the item text, asset name, frequency badge and findings fields. That would have proved the sheet's chrome fits, not the sheet. ★AND A FLOW THAT NEVER OPENED IS REPORTED AS UNREACHED, NEVER AS CLEAN: the first run passed page.evaluate three arguments where it takes one, and every flow errored - counted as an instrument failure, which is why the run did not read as three tidy surfaces. Read-only: it opens and closes, never saves. ★AND FOR AN OVERLAY THE EDGE THAT MATTERS IS THE BOTTOM (T17 added 2026-08-27): the level-up card is a CENTRED FIXED overlay, so a card taller than a 320x844 phone puts its only dismiss button below the fold, and because the overlay does not scroll there is no gesture that reaches it - the reward moment becomes a trap. Driven through showLevelUpModal() with a REAL achievement id so the card carries its badge, heading and tier line, since an empty overlay is a different height. The bottom axis is checked only where a flow asks for it, because an ordinary PAGE is meant to extend past the fold - that is what scrolling is for - and flagging that everywhere would drown the finding. PROACTIVE guard (the property holds today), so its teeth are synthetic negatives, one per independent failure mode, all six verified: an off-screen control, a required control that is absent, a surface that does not exist, the real sheet clean at the floor, an off-BOTTOM control caught when the flow asks, and the bottom NOT checked when it does not - that last one proves the flag actually gates the check rather than being ignored. A width negative alone is NOT sufficient - at --width 200 the handover went RED while both PM sheets still passed.

CF: the signup notice may only claim what was actually linked (2026-08-26). After creating an account index.html could announce 'Your existing records as <name> are now linked to your account' - and it decided that by COUNTING v_worker_truth rows matching the display name. That view exposes worker_profiles.display_name and is security_invoker, so under RLS a brand-new user can see exactly ONE row: the profile the very same flow inserted moments earlier. ★MEASURED on a fresh identity with no hive: c2_count = 1, visible_rows = 1 - so the count was always >= 1 and EVERY new signup was told their existing records had been linked. For someone who had none that is false; for a namesake it claims another person's work history, which is the same identity-by-name trap that let a second Juan Dela Cruz be refused a hive. ★THE CHECK AND THE ACTION READ DIFFERENT ROWS: the reassurance was computed from PROFILE rows while the actual linking is done by resolveActiveHiveContext(), which reads MEMBERSHIP. The notice now rests on that function's return value - non-null exactly when a membership was found and linked - and NAMES the hive it landed in, so the claim says what it rests on. ★THE GATE RUNS THE DB HALF LIVE rather than only reading the page, because the page assertion alone would not explain itself: it re-seeds a membership-less identity and re-measures the self-match, so if that count ever stops being 1 the gate says the PREMISE changed instead of passing quietly.

I-pillar: which hive a session is seated in is decided by AUTH, not by a name (2026-08-26). resolveActiveHiveContext() in index.html chooses the tenant a signed-in session lands in, and it selected memberships with .eq('worker_name', displayName) - where worker_name in v_worker_truth is worker_profiles.display_name. So the query asked 'which memberships belong to this NAME' and depended entirely on the profiles_read_own RLS policy (auth_uid = auth.uid()) to turn that into 'which memberships are MINE'. ★CORRECT, AND FOR THE WRONG REASON - which is the whole point: measured, a caller sees exactly ONE profile row, so the name filter could only ever match themselves and there was no live defect. But the safety lived in the POLICY, not in the query, and widening profile reads even slightly - a co-member roster is an ordinary thing to want - would have let a NAMESAKE's memberships resolve here and seated a person in a hive they do not belong to. The view already joins membership on hm.auth_uid = wp.auth_uid, so the name filter bought nothing the identity does not buy more safely. Verified no behaviour change on a real multi-hive account: both filters return the same two memberships. ★THIS IS THE THIRD FACE OF ONE DEFECT, all found the same day: a hive join that refused a second Juan Dela Cruz by unique index, a signup notice that counted its own freshly-written profile row, and a tenant seat chosen by name. A name is not an identity. ★BOTH HALVES ARE ASSERTED because either can rot: the page must filter by identity AND worker_profiles SELECT must still be self-scoped - if that policy widens, the gate says so rather than passing quietly, since that widening is precisely what would have made the old code dangerous. An unknown identity must mean SOLO MODE, never a name guess. Teeth: reverting the filter to worker_name goes RED on both assertions.

T8: re-authenticating costs one sign-in, not your place (2026-08-26). When a token expires, session-timeout.js sends the worker to index.html?signin=1&return=<where they were>, and index.html validates that value before honouring it - an open-redirect guard, and the right instinct. But the guard's character class did not include characters the platform's OWN pages write into their URLs. ★MEASURED BY ROUND-TRIPPING THE REAL CHAIN (page writes filter -> session-timeout captures -> index re-reads): URLSearchParams.set() encodes a space as '+', and audit-log.html mirrors its filters into the URL including `actor`, which is a worker's NAME - so `audit-log.html?actor=Leandro+Marquez` and `audit-log.html?q=pump+seal` both failed the guard and were dropped IN SILENCE, landing the supervisor on the dashboard. That is T28's exact scenario, someone mid-investigation into who changed what, losing their place to a token refresh with nothing on screen explaining why. ★WHY WIDENING TO + , : IS SAFE, ARGUED NOT ASSUMED: the guard's job is to refuse a scheme, a protocol-relative //, and a foreign absolute path, and its ANCHOR already requires the value to begin with <name>.html or /workhive/ - so those three can only appear AFTER the ? or #, where a colon cannot read as a scheme and a plus is just a space. The gate proves both halves rather than trusting the argument: 8 real destinations survive AND 10 attack shapes (javascript:, //evil.com, https://, ../../, backslash-UNC, index.html@evil.com) are still refused. ★IT EXTRACTS THE REGEX FROM index.html instead of restating it, because a gate holding its own copy proves only that the copy is fine - and it FAILS IF THE THREE GUARDS DISAGREE (sign-in, signup, entry bridge), since a fix reaching one path and not the others is how this class survives. Teeth proven on both: the pre-fix class resurrects the two dropped destinations, and reverting a SINGLE guard is caught as disagreement.

T8: the sign-in screen says WHY the worker is looking at it (2026-08-26). A worker mid-task looks up and finds a sign-in modal with no explanation, which is indistinguishable from being logged out at random - and the question in their head goes unanswered: did I lose what I was doing? ★ONE FUNCTION, THREE EVENTS, THREE DIFFERENT TRUTHS: session-timeout.js's clearIdentityHard() runs for an automatic idle timeout, for the worker deliberately pressing Sign out, AND (via the storage listener) for a sign-out in another tab. Telling someone who just pressed Sign out that their session 'timed out' is false, so the reason is now a parameter, the deliberate path passes none, and the gate asserts that separation - collapsing it is the easy mistake, and passing clearIdentityHard straight to addEventListener would make the click EVENT the reason. ★THE REAL ASSERTION IS THE CLAIM'S PRECONDITION, NOT THE WORDING: the notice tells an idle-timed-out worker 'your drafts are still here', which is true ONLY because clearIdentityHard wipes identity keys alone (wh_last_worker + the hive keys) and never touches whAutoSaveDraft storage. Add a draft key to that wipe list and the copy silently becomes a lie no test would catch - so the gate READS the wipe list and fails on anything draft-shaped. A claim has to rest on something; this is the something. ★AND THE COPY IS A WHITELIST, NOT INTERPOLATION: ?reason= comes from the URL, so it is looked up in a fixed table and written with textContent, and an unknown value renders NOTHING - verified live across four cases (idle and othertab show; a deliberate sign-in and a nonsense reason stay silent). role=status so a screen-reader user is told too. Teeth proven on all three.

T124: the printed page must not be the dark theme (2026-08-26). Plants run on paper - a PM schedule goes on the noticeboard, an audit trail into a folder for DOLE - and this platform is DARK. Printed without rules that is either a black sheet that empties a cartridge or, because most browsers drop backgrounds, pale grey text nobody can read. Neither failure appears anywhere ON SCREEN, which is exactly why it needs a gate: print CSS is invisible until it has already wasted someone's trip to the printer. MEASURED: the three pages a plant demonstrably prints already do this properly - white sheet, #111 text, the reset applied to DESCENDANTS (each card and chip carries its own dark background, so a rule on body alone leaves them), the hub/FAB/toasts/dialogs/buttons hidden, and page-break-inside on cards and table rows. This is a RATCHET over work already done, and the held set may not SHRINK - deleting the rules is not a way to pass. ★ITS FIRST VERSION MANUFACTURED FIVE FINDINGS AND ALL FIVE WERE WRONG, which is the part worth keeping: (1) it treated every @media print block as a claim to be printable, but asset-hub's block says in its own comment that it exists so the rule is 'reachable from document.styleSheets' for a DIFFERENT gate, and the report pages already render as light document panels where a dark-to-light reset would be redundant; (2) it read only the FIRST print block, and analytics-report carries SIX - the first being a one-line rule about a field's min-height - so five pages were graded on whichever rule sorted earliest; (3) its skip-list matched substrings against the ABSOLUTE path, and this project lives under '.../Self-learning Road-Map/...', which contains 'learn' - so it excluded EVERY page and reported '0 printable pages examined' while still failing. Three instrument errors before one true reading. ★AND ITS PASS LINE OVERSTATED until corrected: it claimed all 8 pages met the contract when only 3 are held. Teeth proven on a weakened rule AND on deletion.

T99: a comma in a search box must not 400 the read (2026-08-26). MEASURED against the live REST endpoint: or=(machine.ilike.*bearing, spherical*,...) returns HTTP 400, 'failed to parse logic tree'. PostgREST's or=(a,b) grammar splits on top-level commas, so an unquoted comma inside a value ends the condition early and the ENTIRE filter is rejected; parentheses do the same. ★THE TERM THAT BREAKS IT IS THE ORDINARY ONE: 'Bearing, spherical roller, 22320 E1 XL C3, SKF' is how a real part is named - it is this platform's OWN example in the longest-truncates gate - and typing it into the logbook feed, the logbook EXPORT, community, or the global search overlay produced a 400 the page renders as a FAILED READ. A legitimate search looked like an outage, which is worse than no results: the worker concludes the system is down and stops looking. ★TWO DIFFERENT JOBS, AND ONLY ONE WAS BEING DONE. Escaping % and _ stops a wildcard changing WHICH rows match; removing the delimiters stops the filter failing to parse at all. FOUR sites did the first and not the second. marketplace.html was the exception - it strips them - which is why the same phrase worked there and nowhere else, and why nobody had noticed. ★FIXED CENTRALLY with whSafeSearchTerm (delimiters removed, wildcards escaped, capped), applied at all four sites. Delimiters are REMOVED rather than escaped because PostgREST offers no escape for them inside an unquoted value, and a space keeps word boundaries so the phrase still matches. VERIFIED END TO END: the same read that returned 400 now returns 200 with an empty array - an honest no-match instead of an error. ★AND THE SAME BUG WAS IN THE EDGE FUNCTIONS, where it is WORSE because it is SILENT. agentic-rag-loop's logbook lane sanitises a natural-language QUESTION - where commas are not an edge case but the common case - and read the result as `const { data: logs } = await q`, DESTRUCTURING THE ERROR AWAY. supabase-js RETURNS {data:null,error} rather than throwing, so the rejected filter never reached the surrounding catch and `logs || []` turned a 400 into an ordinary empty result: the AI answered with less grounding and nothing anywhere said why. Its comment reads 'Escape LIKE wildcards in user input (per data-engineer skill)' - the author followed the skill exactly, and the skill covered wildcards but not delimiters. visual-defect-capture passed an asset TAG into an .or() with no escaping at all. Both fixed, and the error is now logged instead of discarded. The gate covers the edge functions too, including the `const { data } = await q` shape that makes the failure invisible. Teeth proven on four clauses: the helper weakened, a page interpolating a raw term, an edge fn dropping the delimiter strip, and an edge fn discarding the error again.

T38: typed work must outlive a session expiry (2026-08-27). A worker half-fills a logbook entry, the token dies, they sign in again - and whether their typing is still there depends on a three-link chain no single file makes visible, with every link in a different place: whAutoSaveDraft persists the text; session-timeout's clearIdentityHard wipes the IDENTITY keys and must not touch draft keys; and the draft is restored only to the worker who typed it, by an OWNER CHECK that reads wh_last_worker - the very key the expiry just deleted. ★SO THE DRAFT SURVIVES ONLY BECAUSE RE-AUTH PUTS THAT KEY BACK. Sign-in rewrites wh_last_worker, so by the time the worker returns the owner check matches again and the text reappears. Re-key that check to something sign-in does NOT restore and every draft on the platform is silently discarded after an expiry: the form comes back empty and nothing explains it. That is the assertion - the key the owner check reads must be one the sign-in path writes. ★THE OWNER CHECK IS NOT THE BUG, it is the shared-tablet protection: worker A's draft must not appear in worker B's form. Removing it would 'fix' the expiry case by leaking someone's typing to the next person on the device, which is worse. ★AND THE ASSERTION HAD TO BE 'AT LEAST ONE LINK', NOT 'EVERY LINK': the check is a fallback chain (wh_last_worker || wh_worker_name) and utils.js records that the alias reads are dead - 'never written anywhere in the codebase (get-without-set)'. Demanding every link be restored flagged that dead alias and called a working chain broken. Teeth proven on both clauses: sign-in ceasing to restore the key, and an expiry that starts wiping a draft key.

T101: 100% of the money risk sits at one step (2026-08-27). This is a CONTACT-ONLY marketplace - no escrow, no held funds, no reversal - so a buyer contacts a stranger and pays them off-platform, and every peso of risk lives at that single moment. RA 11967, the PH Internet Transactions Act, requires consumer education on the red flags in internet transactions, which makes this a legal floor as well as a decent one. ★STATING A FACT IS NOT WARNING: 'payment is off-platform' is true and tells a buyer nothing about what to DO. The page carries an actual warning at the decision point - inspect the item, meet at the seller's business address or a public place, avoid paying in full up front to a new seller - and the sentence that sets expectations correctly: WorkHive never holds your payment, so we cannot reverse it. ★THE OPPOSITE FAILURE IS WORSE THAN SILENCE, so the gate also refuses escrow / buyer-protection / money-back / guaranteed-refund language on the marketplace surfaces: a buyer who believes there is protection behaves as though a loss is recoverable. It strips COMMENTS before matching, so prose ABOUT a promise is not read as the promise. ★AND IT HOLDS TWO SUBTLE CLAIMS THE PAGE ALREADY GOT RIGHT: 'credits back' must carry that credits are spend-only and cannot be withdrawn, because the bare words read like money returning; and the trust bar must say 'ID-Verified badge per seller' rather than 'ID-Verified Sellers', which as a bare heading reads as a property of the RESULTS - the same false claim the source chip carried when 3 of 9 listings actually had a verified seller. Teeth proven on the removed reversal sentence and on an introduced protection promise.

T28: an audit nobody can reach is write-only (2026-08-27). 'Who changed this?' is asked while looking at the RECORD - an asset whose details are wrong, a reported post, a decision someone disputes. If the only way in is to know the page exists and open it cold, the trail is technically complete and practically useless: the supervisor gives up or goes to SQL, and the compliance story the platform tells about itself is one nobody can walk. ★A LINK THAT DROPS THE RECORD IS BARELY BETTER - arriving at an unfiltered log of every power action while holding the id in your head is the same scavenger hunt with extra steps. So BOTH ends are asserted: the links must carry the subject (asset-hub sends ?q=<tag>, community sends ?action=report_post) AND audit-log must CONSUME those parameters, or the context is written into the URL and thrown away - a promise only the sender believes, which is the declared-but-never-wired class. MEASURED: two context-carrying links, audit-log consumes all four of q/actor/action/target. ★THE HIVE MENU ENTRY DOES NOT SATISFY THIS: audit-log is a hidden page, so a menu item makes it reachable only to someone who already knows to look; the record-level affordances are what make it findable at the moment the question is actually asked, which is why bare links are reported but do not count toward the requirement. Teeth proven on both halves - links stripped of their record, and the audit page ceasing to read what it is sent.

T3/T154: the markdown twin must say what the page says (2026-08-27). Every public page ships a clean twin at <page>.md - the llms.txt convention, served deliberately (_headers: 'Markdown twins ... every page also exists at <page>.md') so answer engines read structured text instead of scraping markup. That makes the twin a PUBLISHING CHANNEL, and a stale one is worse than none: an agent fetching it gets a confident, well-formed, WRONG version of the page. ★MEASURED 2026-08-27: 107 of 119 twins had DRIFTED, including privacy-policy and terms-of-service - an answer engine could quote retired legal text. The sharpest instance was T3's recorded defect surviving in the machine channel after being fixed in the human one: 60 calculator twins still said 'free, no sign-up needed' on a link INTO engineering-design.html, which redirects to sign-in, while the HTML had already been corrected to 'A free account takes about 30 seconds'. Zero served pages carried the claim; sixty twins did. ★THE VALIDATOR ALREADY EXISTED AND WORKED - tools/validate_md_twins.py, with a source_sha per twin and the right reasoning in its own docstring - and NOTHING RAN IT: it appeared in no gate registration, the same orphaned-prover shape as the three unreferenced provers found earlier this session. A working oracle nobody runs is indistinguishable from one never written. Fixed by rebuilding (118 rebuilt, 119/119 current, 0 twins still carrying the claim) and by REGISTERING the validator, so the next HTML edit that forgets the twin fails here instead of shipping a confident wrong answer to a machine. FIX ON FAIL: python tools/build_md_twins.py. ★NOW IN --fast (2026-09-11): registering the gate was only half the repair - it was registered skip_if_fast, and the discipline this project actually runs is '--fast at milestones, the full board is Ian's ~6h gate'. So this gate was structurally unrun for the ENTIRE duration of every edit wave, which is precisely when twin drift is created. Measured today: one card blurb on learn/index sent me into the generated mirror, and the rebuild reported 117 of 120 twins ALREADY DRIFTED from the day's earlier edits - 117 public pages serving a confident, well-formed, wrong copy of themselves to answer engines, with no milestone check able to see it. The validator costs 1.98s. skip_if_fast is for expensive gates; a 2-second check guarding a PUBLISHING CHANNEL earns nothing by being skipped and loses a whole wave of visibility. A registered gate that never runs in the mode you actually run is the orphaned-prover shape one layer up - [[feedback_three_ways_a_lock_is_hollow]].

Night Crawler distill quality guard self-test (tools/night_crawler.py --selftest — deterministic, no network/AI, instant). UFAI experience-in-motion source-grep dims (2026-07-22, PDDA_UX_PAINPOINT_JOURNEY_ROADMAP) — the 3 journey dims the runtime __RUBRIC lens can't cleanly see, measured from page SOURCE + forward-ratcheted: J3 consequence (every destructive handler routes through the shared whConfirm OR is soft-delete-undoable — NN/g 'undo > confirmation'), G5 system-memory (a filterable page persists the user's filter/view/sort choice to localStorage), S4 behavioral-consistency (destructive actions use the ONE shared whConfirm, no raw window.confirm). D12 per-SURFACE AI cost/quota adoption (2026-07-23, the D-ledger's 'per-surface oracle unbuilt' cell, now built). `ai_rate_limits` is keyed by hive_id ALONE - one hourly+daily budget shared by EVERY AI surface - so a single runaway surface (looping companion, batch brief, retry storm) can drain the hive's whole AI allowance and starve assistant/voice/RAG/report-gen. The per-surface limiter ALREADY EXISTS (`_shared/rate-limit.ts` checkRouteRateLimit -> hive_route_quotas.hourly_cap + hive_route_calls counter keyed by (hive,route,hour), with an `enforce` flag so a surface can onboard in LOG-ONLY mode first) - so this is an ADOPTION gap, the METHOD-LAW shape (one unadopted central component, not N bespoke fixes). Currently 2/19 = 10.5% (ai-gateway, platform-gateway). Forward-only ratchet: a NEW rate-limited AI surface wired to the global cap alone drops the % and FAILs. Measurement only - changes no enforcement. Self-test: --selftest.

UFAI U-pillar deep-verification lock (2026-07-23, PDDA §11 comprehensive deepwalk) — the live per-page deep-probe found the coarse A-Z lens (Z3 = 24px WCAG floor) was blind to the deeper UFAI U2 field standard (44px gloved-hand tap goal) + the Z2d responsive-image floor. Three comparison pages (workhive-vs-maintainx, workhive-vs-upkeep, best-free-cmms-software-philippines) carry 26 dollar figures belonging to vendors we do not control. Each already makes the right promise in its own words — 'Pricing verified against vendor and directory listings on 5 August 2026 ... This comparison is REVIEWED QUARTERLY for pricing and feature accuracy' — and NOTHING ENFORCED EITHER the date or the cadence. That is the shape this project has already been burned by: a step that depends on somebody remembering does not happen (v_kpi_truth's hourly refresh shipped as a root 'run this manually' file). The failure mode is specific: a competitor raises its price, our page keeps quoting the old one, and a comparison that was accurate when written becomes a misleading claim about another company's product — worse to be wrong about than our own. The gate parses each page's own stated date and cadence and fails when the page outlives its own promise, or when a named vendor's price carries no date at all. ★SCOPE IS PROXIMITY, NOT CO-OCCURRENCE, and that was learned the hard way: the first version scoped in any page where a brand appeared anywhere and a price appeared anywhere, and immediately produced a FALSE POSITIVE — the platform guide names Fiix as an INTEGRATION TARGET in one table row and quotes a generic 'often around $20 to $50 per user per month' in another, and neither is a claim about Fiix's price. A brand and a figure must now sit within 200 characters of each other, and that exact page is pinned as an out-of-scope assertion. Generic category prices with no vendor attached ('paid products commonly start around $20', 'an analyzer can range from $5,000 to $10,000') stay out of scope deliberately. MEASURED 2026-09-21: 3 pages in scope, all dated 5 August 2026 on a quarterly cadence, 47 of 92 days — registers GREEN and begins failing on 3 November 2026.
